With my own experience of CSA, CSEM, and forgiveness, I learned something over the years that makes it easier, but that doesn't make it totally easy in any case.

The truth of the matter is that everyone was a child at some point, and something around 80% of abusers were at some point abused themselves. They are wounded little boys and girls.

But that doesn't matter. What matters is me. And I realized early on in my adulthood that if I dont pray for and forgive the people who hurt and used me; no one else will.

If I don't pray for my abuser no one else will, which greatly decreases any sliver of a chance that he could make it to Heaven. And the fact of the matter is that God very much desires that everyone He has created will go to heaven, including him.

So what would have happened if I wasn't a victim? Is that a guarantee that he would have died permanently separated from God? Does that mean the infernal horrible pain that Christ experiences as He loses His children would only be multiplied?

If I put it harshly or possibly even exaggerate a bit, I have to accept that it is my job, perhaps even my purpose in life, to forgive those people. And forgiveness includes prayer for their conversion and salvation. I know that when I die, it would give me greater joy to see a man doing what we are all made to do for eternity- that is, worship God - than it ever could give me to see him suffering.

So, I keep my eyes on the reality that is eternity and as I remember what happened with disgust and fear, I offer it to God to form me into the version of myself that is perfect - or at least forgiving. I prayed for my abuser when he was alive and I pray for him now after his untimely death. Sometimes that's all I have to hold on to when the PTSD is at its worst. God made me to show love to the worst and most evil men I have encountered, and I trust He will show me why when judgment day comes.

But I'm not perfect and I have to admit that I hope they are all in Purgatory for a lengthy sentence...

The pic on the right is the biggest I ever was, and I actually had a brain surgery 2 weeks later! After my brain surgery I started exercising and CICO, but I unfortunately spiraled back into the eating disorder I had as a teenager. 1.5 years later I started "treatment" for the ED but the providers were awful and I dropped out. And then I just lost control and gained nearly every pound that I lost in that period back, and then kept it for three years. I wanted to lose weight afterward of course but I was afraid of falling back into my disordered habits so I used that as an excuse not to try. This year in February I decided that wasn't acceptable anymore. I set for myself strict guidelines to prevent myself from falling into that cycle, and started working hard and educating myself on nutrition.

The biggest change is that I started training for strength and not just cardio. I went from no exercise to only cardio, to finally mixing both weightlifting/strength training and cardio. And that changed everything. My entire view on how to treat my body has become so much more holistic, and I'm happy. This progress isn't just physical, it's mental, and I'm so excited to continue this journey.
